title: Unit 1 - My family, my friends & me

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 1
parts.instructions: Read the three texts about families. For each question, choose the correct answer.

persons.name: Leo
persons.text: There are a lot of us in my family, and I love it. Our house is crowded, so I'm never alone or bored. I've got a brother and three sisters. My brother and I have one bedroom, and my sisters have another. Mum and Dad work a lot, and my grandparents live near us, so they often look after us when my parents are working. My grandfather is from France, and he sometimes helps me with my French homework.

persons.name: Bastian
persons.text: I live with my mum, dad and brother. My brother and I have our own bedrooms. He's only a year older than me, so we do lots of things together, which is fun. We've got an aunt and uncle who live in the same street as us, together with their daughter – our cousin – and our grandparents. Dad works in an office, and Mum is a teacher. She was born in Italy, but she came to live here in the USA a long time ago.

persons.name: Callum
persons.text: My family is big, but we don't all live in the same place. I have cousins in Germany and Australia, so I don't see them very often. My parents, my sister and I share a house with my grandma, but my sister and I have our own bedrooms. Mum and Dad go out to work, and they don't have much free time, so sometimes I tidy up the house. Mum likes it when I do that.

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

persons.name: Shaziye
persons.text: I live with my parents in the city of Bursa, Turkey, and both my mother's and my father's parents live in a village by the sea not far from us. When they were younger, my father's parents lived and worked in Bulgaria. They were both teachers, and came back to Turkey when they finished work. I'm glad we all live in the same country now because we can see each other every week. I love their village, but they always get up very early and I do as well when I stay there. That's not easy for me!

persons.name: Frida
persons.text: Six people live in my house in the city of Leon, Mexico. My mother's mother, my parents, my two brothers and me. I'm really lucky because my father's parents also live in a street near our flat, so I visit them nearly every day, too. I call my mother's mother Bela. She had a restaurant and now cooks fantastic meals for us. Mum can't cook well, but I can because Bela's teaching me.

persons.name: Agata
persons.text: I often visit my father's parents because they live close to us. But my mother's parents are travelling around the world so it's not possible to go and see them. We often chat on the internet. My father's father works ten hours every week. He's a doctor, so we always phone him when we feel ill. My father's mother was also a doctor, but she doesn't work now. I have lunch with her on Saturdays.

parts.title: Listening Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear Kelly talking to her mum about her singing lessons.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Kelly, I spoke to your singing teacher last night. You haven't got a lesson this week.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: OK, so when's my next lesson?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: It'll be on the <u>15th of August</u> – you're missing this week, which is the 8th of August, and on the 22nd of August, your teacher's away again.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: Right.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: She said you need a new music book, too.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: Oh, OK. Where can we get that?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Well, they haven't got any music at the library, I've looked before. <u>The bookshop</u>'s cheaper than the music shop, so we'll get it there.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: OK.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Which day shall we go?

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: How about <u>Thursday</u>? You work late on Tuesdays and I've got dance club on Wednesday.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Fine.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: Will you pick me up after school?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: No, I only finish work at quarter to four, so go home first. I'll see you there at <u>four o'clock</u>. Then we'll get to the shop about quarter past four.

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: Right.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Would you like dinner in a restaurant afterwards?

script.speaker: Kelly
script.text: Yeah! I heard the burger restaurant's closed, but I'd like to go and have a <u>pizza</u>. The fish restaurant's a bit too far from the shops.

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Great!

parts.title: Listening Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear Simon talking to his friend Amanda about his school day.

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: Hi, Simon! How are you?

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: Oh hi, Amanda! I'm tired!

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: Me too! (1) I <u>go to sleep really late</u> because my brother watches TV in his room, and I can hear it.

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: Oh, that's a shame! But you don't have to get up really early, like I do!

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: Get up really early? Why's that?

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: I take the boat to school now. (2) It goes at <u>half past seven</u>, so Mum wakes us up at a quarter past six. We have breakfast and leave home at seven.

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: So you've changed schools?

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: Yes. The school on our island is for six to eleven year olds. (3) Now <u>I'm twelve</u>, I go to school on another island with my sister Tanya. She's fourteen now.

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: Oh. What about getting home?

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: The boat goes two hours after school finishes. (4) <u>Mum's sister lives near the school</u> so we have dinner there.

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: So that's your school day! (5) <u>It's not like mine – much more interesting</u> – and longer!

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: It's what everyone my age on the island does.

script.speaker: Amanda
script.text: Some people probably think it's fun, or even exciting, but I don't like boats.

script.speaker: Simon
script.text: Well, it's the only way!
